Supermicro booked $60 billion in new orders and targets $72 billion in revenue, yet Wall Street still rates it a near-sell. Here is what analysts are missing and the three conditions that could send shares to $70 by 2027.
Published October 6, 2026, 12:00pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI | SMCI Price Prediction | SMCI Price Prediction) wants to be more than a server assembler. The San Jose company booked more than $60 billion in new orders last quarter. It now targets fiscal 2027 revenue of $65 billion to $72 billion, up from $39.1 billion in fiscal 2026.
Shares are up 48.31% year to date and still trade at about 10x forward earnings. That gap raises the question of whether Supermicro can hit $70 per share in 2027.
What’s Holding Supermicro Back Below Its 52-Week High
The stock has momentum: shares rose 4.58% over the past week and 18.25% over the past month. Even so, they are still down 17.14% over the past year.
Credibility weighs on the stock, as revenue missed estimates in five of the last six quarters. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow came in at negative $6.8 billion, and the company raised $5.6 billion in equity.
Q1 gross margin guidance of 10.4% to 10.8% sits far below Q4’s 17.6%. An update on the board inquiry is still pending. The stock’s beta is 1.996, so each of these worries hits shares roughly twice as hard as the broader market.
Wall Street Sees No Upside. Our Model Says 12.4%
The consensus target is $42.38, about 2.4% below today’s $43.41. Analysts rate it 2 Strong Buys, 3 Buys, 11 Holds, 2 Sells and 1 Strong Sell. Our base case is $48.78, or 12.4% upside. The model’s range runs from $37.60 in the bear case to $53.54 in the bull case, and confidence is high at 0.9.
In my view, analysts are stuck on to old disappointments. Only 26% of them are bullish. In our adjustment, earnings growth contributed 0.03, five times the 0.006 from analyst views. Fundamentals are improving faster than the ratings.
Here’s What It Takes for Supermicro to Reach $70
Getting to $70 from the current $43.41 calls for a 61.3% gain. Forward EPS is $4.3382, so $70 equals to a forward P/E of 16x. Our base case already implies 12x, which means the bold target needs 5x of additional multiple expansion.
That seems achievable. Forward EPS already exceeds fiscal 2026’s $3.63, so the forward multiple falls if guidance holds. Enterprise and channel revenue rose 172% to $5.6 billion in Q4.
CEO Charles Liang said “we are improving profitability through a richer enterprise customer mix and broader adoption of our optimized Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) architecture.”
Supermicro is one of the picks-and-shovels names behind the AI data-center expansion (we covered seven of these suppliers, from power to cooling, in a report you can download here). The main risk is that power and cooling delays push backlog shipments into later quarters.
Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh raised the firm’s price target on Super Micro to $43 from $35 and keeps a Neutral rating on the shares.
Supermicro Trades at a Discount to Its Earnings Power
At $43.41, shares trade at 10x forward EPS. That looks cheap for a business that grew revenue 78%, though cash flow concerns explain part of the discount.
Shares range from a 52-week low of $19.48 to a high of $58.78. Over 10 years, the stock has returned 1,748.02%. A $70 price would still leave Supermicro at a mid-teens multiple.
$70 Is a Stretch, but Here’s Why It’s Possible
Reaching $70 in 2027 calls for a 61.3% advance. I see it as a stretch that is still within reach. Three conditions must be met. First, record backlog has to convert into revenue near the top of guidance.
Second, gross margins need to hold as the enterprise and DCBBS mix grows. Third, operating cash flow has to turn positive without more dilution. Another revenue miss or a bad board inquiry outcome would ruin it. Investors shouldn’t expect this level of return every year, but we’ve outlined the plan for how Super Micro Computer could reach $70 in 2027.

Three key insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series
AI storage strategy is taking on a larger role as enterprises move from successful experiments to systems that must deliver dependable business results. How organizations store, serve and manage data increasingly shapes the performance, cost and practicality of artificial intelligence deployments.
The challenge extends beyond choosing faster hardware. Evolving workloads require enterprises to rethink how their infrastructure supports data-intensive applications. Turning that infrastructure into a production foundation requires coordination across the organization, according to theCUBE Research’s Rob Strechay.
“The organizations succeeding today are focusing less on models and more on operationalization,” Strechay said. “They’re aligning data teams, infrastructure teams and business stakeholders around measurable outcomes and repeatable deployment strategies.”
During the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series, industry leaders examined the evolution of storage architectures to meet those production demands. Their discussions explored what it takes to build an efficient, adaptable foundation for enterprise AI. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the event:
Insight #1: AI storage strategy changes the economics of inference.
Keeping graphics processing units productive requires storage that can serve active workloads quickly while accommodating growing volumes of less frequently accessed data. An effective AI storage strategy balances those demands across performance and capacity tiers, pointed out Greg DiFraia, senior vice president of AI and alliance partnerships at Scality Inc.
“We need to drive utilization up as high as it can go, and in order to do that, you’ve got to really think about things differently,” he said. “Because when we look at the topology for customers, it’s that the life cycle, when you’re talking about tens or hundreds of petabytes or even exabytes, it’s not all going to live in flash.”
Expanding agent contexts are also creating demand for storage that stores intermediate calculations used during inference. When those key-value caches outgrow GPU memory, additional tiers must balance capacity with fast access. Solidigm Inc.’s flash drives, Super Micro Computer Inc.’s integrated systems and Vast Data Inc.’s data platform support this evolving hierarchy, emphasized Anat Heilper, director of AI architecture at Vast Data.
“When we talk about [key-value] cache, which is a very significant optimization that can be done in AI inferencing … in essence, it’s the ability to replace compute with storage,” she told theCUBE. “When you have very high KV cache hit rates, we both save on compute and reduce the latency significantly.”
Insight #2: Production AI requires workload-specific systems and operational controls.
Production infrastructure must support the business decisions organizations need to make. In financial services, the speed of data processing can affect risk assessment and capital availability, noted Moiz Kohari, vice president of enterprise AI and data intelligence at DataDirect Networks Inc., who spoke alongside Vince Chen, senior director of solutions architecture at Supermicro.
“If you’re a company like BlackRock or State Street where you’re looking at a trillion dollars on your books and you have 6% to 12% capital lockup, that’s a big deal,” Kohari said. “You’re carrying that risk on your books. We can do those calculations because we can move that data back and forth quickly. When you do that, you’re unlocking 6% of that capital, so that capital can be leveraged to do anything else.”
Meeting those requirements also means assembling components that work together at the required scale. Supermicro’s partner approach addresses that deployment burden through integrated configurations, according to Chen.
“For the enterprise customers to build the AI factory as an AI purpose-built infrastructure, there has been complexity in that,” he said. “What we are doing here is working with our partners to build vertically integrated and then pre-validated T-shirt size options for our customers to choose from.”
Deployment is only the beginning of the operational challenge. As pilots become production services, organizations must accommodate broader usage within infrastructure limits, explained Ruhi Sehgal, agentic AI solutions marketing lead at Nutanix Inc.
“But with this shift comes a new dynamic we know all too well, which is we have highly constrained resources that need to be shared by a massive set of new users,” she said. “How do I ensure resilience? What infrastructure admins do every day — which is managing multi-tenancy, ensuring security [and] optimizing performance — that’s exactly what AI needs.”
Insight #3: Enterprise data becomes useful through access, orchestration and governance.
An AI storage strategy must make enterprise data usable across applications while keeping it available. Lakehouse architectures built around open formats provide a foundation for connecting traditional analytics and newer AI workflows. MinIO Inc.’s AIStor supports Apache Iceberg tables and the Iceberg REST catalog, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s processors and Supermicro systems supply the underlying compute, memory and connectivity. Bringing those capabilities together gives organizations more flexibility in putting their data to work, pointed out Greg DeMichillie, vice president of product and technical marketing at MinIO.
“On the data lake side, I think it’s hard to overstate just what a big deal Iceberg has been,” he told theCUBE. “If you think back, it’s not that long ago that every database had its own proprietary format. The idea of an open table format was just bonkers … but we are really seeing now the incredible widespread adoption. That’s enabled us to do really clever things like integrating support for Iceberg into the storage tier.”
That flexibility must extend to documents, images, logs and other unstructured information spread across the enterprise. Coordinating access and movement across the data estate requires several complementary layers: Supermicro’s validated systems, Hammerspace Inc.’s unified namespace and data orchestration, Cloudian Inc.’s object storage and Seagate Technology LLC’s capacity for longer-term retention. Together, those components support a data life cycle spanning active AI use and archival storage, emphasized Sherry Lin, senior product manager of SDS solution at Supermicro. Governance remains essential throughout that life cycle, noted Peter Sjoberg, vice president of worldwide solution architects at Cloudian.
“We see a key goal to put that unstructured data under management so that it is protected, it is safe and secure,” Sjoberg said. “That’s exactly what we’re doing now as this data has moved into the AI era. That data will need to move for different purposes, and you will need to make sure it’s always under your control, unstructured or otherwise, so that you can bring it to your AI needs.”

Supermicro's gross margin just shattered expectations, sending shares surging, but management quietly buried a number in the earnings call that changes everything investors think they just bought.
Published September 8, 2026, 7:10am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Rows of illuminated servers in a data center symbolize the robust AI infrastructure provided by companies like Super Micro Computer, critical for advancing technological frontiers. © BalticServers.com
Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI | SMCI Price Prediction) closed most recently at $39.59, up 25.8% over one month and 27.9% year to date, yet still 1.1% lower over the trailing year. The rally traces to a fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 report in which non-GAAP gross margin blew past guidance. Did investors buy a structural margin reset or a one-quarter timing artifact? As it turns out, management answered that question on the earnings call.
The bull case is genuine. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $1.70 against a $0.9575 estimate, revenue grew 93.16% year over year, and CEO Charles Liang cited “more than $60 billion in new orders, and booked record backlog entering fiscal 2027.” Full fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion. Some of last week’s strength was sector-driven; TradingView, on September 4, 2026, headlined the story “Supermicro’s Revenue Boom Just Ran Into a Profit Test.”
Reported non-GAAP gross margin was 17.6% versus guidance of 8.2% to 8.4%, a 750 basis point sequential jump. CFO David Weigand said favorable mix “contributed approximately 75% of the gross margin improvement,” with the remainder attributable to lower tariff costs and lower inventory reserves, which he called a “non-recurring event.” The mix itself was inflated by “the deferral of several contracts from Q4 fiscal year 26 to Q1 fiscal year 27.” Lower-margin revenue slipping out lifts the percentage without improving the business. Liang said, “This margin expansion mainly came from our strategy focused on balancing customer mix and product mix while having a one-time positive contribution for the quarter.” Revenue landed near the low end of the $11 billion to $12.5 billion range on customer readiness delays. Miss on top line, beat on margin, same cause.
Management guided current-quarter non-GAAP gross margin to 10.4% to 10.8%, well below the reported 17.6%. A quiet period begins at the close of business on Friday, September 11, 2026, so this number stands.
Customer diversification is genuine. David Weigand noted nine customers with revenues greater than $1 billion each in fiscal year 2026, versus four in fiscal year 2025. Full-year revenue reached $39.06 billion (+77.8% year over year). (That kind of concentration in AI server buildouts is why we keep pointing readers to the power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the data centers in a free report.)
Offsetting this is that fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was negative $6.81 billion, closing inventory rose to $12.9 billion, and the cash conversion cycle (days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers) lengthened materially. A company can grow revenue while consuming cash when it prepays inventory faster than customers pay invoices.
Supermicro raised $5.6 billion in public equity, including $4.2 billion in mandatory convertible preferred (shares that automatically convert to common). The guided non-GAAP diluted share count is 761 million. David Weigand said EPS is now computed using the two-class method, allocating a portion of net income to participating convertible preferred shares.
Gross margin must hold against the new 10.4% to 10.8% guidance. The deferred contracts must land without dragging margin lower when they do. The $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion revenue range must survive a quarter of contact, and growth must start generating operating cash. This thesis will be disproved by any quarter in which revenue grows and gross margin lands at or below the full prior-year level, or any walk-back of the forward revenue range.
The market bought a margin figure that management, in its own words and its own next-quarter guide, has already told investors will not repeat. Though the growth story is intact and the order book is a genuine asset, the profitability step-up appears transitory.

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.
Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.
Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, Super Micro is expected to post earnings of $1.06 per share, indicating a change of +202.9% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.1% over the last 30 days.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Prediction: The Next Chapter of Supermicro Could Be More Important Than the Last
Supermicro booked $60 billion in new orders and targets $72 billion in revenue, yet Wall Street still rates it a near-sell. Here is what analysts are missing and the three conditions that could send shares to $70 by 2027.
Published October 6, 2026, 12:00pm ET · 3 min read
Price Targets desk. Editor: Vandita Jadeja.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Investing in stocks is a great way to build wealth and gain financial freedom. © Phongphan/Shutterstock.com
Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI | SMCI Price Prediction | SMCI Price Prediction) wants to be more than a server assembler. The San Jose company booked more than $60 billion in new orders last quarter. It now targets fiscal 2027 revenue of $65 billion to $72 billion, up from $39.1 billion in fiscal 2026.
Shares are up 48.31% year to date and still trade at about 10x forward earnings. That gap raises the question of whether Supermicro can hit $70 per share in 2027.
What’s Holding Supermicro Back Below Its 52-Week High
The stock has momentum: shares rose 4.58% over the past week and 18.25% over the past month. Even so, they are still down 17.14% over the past year.
Credibility weighs on the stock, as revenue missed estimates in five of the last six quarters. Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow came in at negative $6.8 billion, and the company raised $5.6 billion in equity.
Q1 gross margin guidance of 10.4% to 10.8% sits far below Q4’s 17.6%. An update on the board inquiry is still pending. The stock’s beta is 1.996, so each of these worries hits shares roughly twice as hard as the broader market.
Wall Street Sees No Upside. Our Model Says 12.4%
The consensus target is $42.38, about 2.4% below today’s $43.41. Analysts rate it 2 Strong Buys, 3 Buys, 11 Holds, 2 Sells and 1 Strong Sell. Our base case is $48.78, or 12.4% upside. The model’s range runs from $37.60 in the bear case to $53.54 in the bull case, and confidence is high at 0.9.
In my view, analysts are stuck on to old disappointments. Only 26% of them are bullish. In our adjustment, earnings growth contributed 0.03, five times the 0.006 from analyst views. Fundamentals are improving faster than the ratings.
Here’s What It Takes for Supermicro to Reach $70
Getting to $70 from the current $43.41 calls for a 61.3% gain. Forward EPS is $4.3382, so $70 equals to a forward P/E of 16x. Our base case already implies 12x, which means the bold target needs 5x of additional multiple expansion.
That seems achievable. Forward EPS already exceeds fiscal 2026’s $3.63, so the forward multiple falls if guidance holds. Enterprise and channel revenue rose 172% to $5.6 billion in Q4.
CEO Charles Liang said “we are improving profitability through a richer enterprise customer mix and broader adoption of our optimized Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) architecture.”
Supermicro is one of the picks-and-shovels names behind the AI data-center expansion (we covered seven of these suppliers, from power to cooling, in a report you can download here). The main risk is that power and cooling delays push backlog shipments into later quarters.
Mizuho analyst Vijay Rakesh raised the firm’s price target on Super Micro to $43 from $35 and keeps a Neutral rating on the shares.
Supermicro Trades at a Discount to Its Earnings Power
At $43.41, shares trade at 10x forward EPS. That looks cheap for a business that grew revenue 78%, though cash flow concerns explain part of the discount.
Shares range from a 52-week low of $19.48 to a high of $58.78. Over 10 years, the stock has returned 1,748.02%. A $70 price would still leave Supermicro at a mid-teens multiple.
$70 Is a Stretch, but Here’s Why It’s Possible
Reaching $70 in 2027 calls for a 61.3% advance. I see it as a stretch that is still within reach. Three conditions must be met. First, record backlog has to convert into revenue near the top of guidance.
Second, gross margins need to hold as the enterprise and DCBBS mix grows. Third, operating cash flow has to turn positive without more dilution. Another revenue miss or a bad board inquiry outcome would ruin it. Investors shouldn’t expect this level of return every year, but we’ve outlined the plan for how Super Micro Computer could reach $70 in 2027.

Coverage from SiliconANGLE's livestreaming video studio
Three key insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series
AI storage strategy is taking on a larger role as enterprises move from successful experiments to systems that must deliver dependable business results. How organizations store, serve and manage data increasingly shapes the performance, cost and practicality of artificial intelligence deployments.
The challenge extends beyond choosing faster hardware. Evolving workloads require enterprises to rethink how their infrastructure supports data-intensive applications. Turning that infrastructure into a production foundation requires coordination across the organization, according to theCUBE Research’s Rob Strechay.
“The organizations succeeding today are focusing less on models and more on operationalization,” Strechay said. “They’re aligning data teams, infrastructure teams and business stakeholders around measurable outcomes and repeatable deployment strategies.”
During the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series, industry leaders examined the evolution of storage architectures to meet those production demands. Their discussions explored what it takes to build an efficient, adaptable foundation for enterprise AI. (* Disclosure below.)
Here are three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the event:
Insight #1: AI storage strategy changes the economics of inference.
Keeping graphics processing units productive requires storage that can serve active workloads quickly while accommodating growing volumes of less frequently accessed data. An effective AI storage strategy balances those demands across performance and capacity tiers, pointed out Greg DiFraia, senior vice president of AI and alliance partnerships at Scality Inc.
“We need to drive utilization up as high as it can go, and in order to do that, you’ve got to really think about things differently,” he said. “Because when we look at the topology for customers, it’s that the life cycle, when you’re talking about tens or hundreds of petabytes or even exabytes, it’s not all going to live in flash.”
Expanding agent contexts are also creating demand for storage that stores intermediate calculations used during inference. When those key-value caches outgrow GPU memory, additional tiers must balance capacity with fast access. Solidigm Inc.’s flash drives, Super Micro Computer Inc.’s integrated systems and Vast Data Inc.’s data platform support this evolving hierarchy, emphasized Anat Heilper, director of AI architecture at Vast Data.
“When we talk about [key-value] cache, which is a very significant optimization that can be done in AI inferencing … in essence, it’s the ability to replace compute with storage,” she told theCUBE. “When you have very high KV cache hit rates, we both save on compute and reduce the latency significantly.”
Insight #2: Production AI requires workload-specific systems and operational controls.
Production infrastructure must support the business decisions organizations need to make. In financial services, the speed of data processing can affect risk assessment and capital availability, noted Moiz Kohari, vice president of enterprise AI and data intelligence at DataDirect Networks Inc., who spoke alongside Vince Chen, senior director of solutions architecture at Supermicro.
“If you’re a company like BlackRock or State Street where you’re looking at a trillion dollars on your books and you have 6% to 12% capital lockup, that’s a big deal,” Kohari said. “You’re carrying that risk on your books. We can do those calculations because we can move that data back and forth quickly. When you do that, you’re unlocking 6% of that capital, so that capital can be leveraged to do anything else.”
Meeting those requirements also means assembling components that work together at the required scale. Supermicro’s partner approach addresses that deployment burden through integrated configurations, according to Chen.
“For the enterprise customers to build the AI factory as an AI purpose-built infrastructure, there has been complexity in that,” he said. “What we are doing here is working with our partners to build vertically integrated and then pre-validated T-shirt size options for our customers to choose from.”
Deployment is only the beginning of the operational challenge. As pilots become production services, organizations must accommodate broader usage within infrastructure limits, explained Ruhi Sehgal, agentic AI solutions marketing lead at Nutanix Inc.
“But with this shift comes a new dynamic we know all too well, which is we have highly constrained resources that need to be shared by a massive set of new users,” she said. “How do I ensure resilience? What infrastructure admins do every day — which is managing multi-tenancy, ensuring security [and] optimizing performance — that’s exactly what AI needs.”
Insight #3: Enterprise data becomes useful through access, orchestration and governance.
An AI storage strategy must make enterprise data usable across applications while keeping it available. Lakehouse architectures built around open formats provide a foundation for connecting traditional analytics and newer AI workflows. MinIO Inc.’s AIStor supports Apache Iceberg tables and the Iceberg REST catalog, while Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s processors and Supermicro systems supply the underlying compute, memory and connectivity. Bringing those capabilities together gives organizations more flexibility in putting their data to work, pointed out Greg DeMichillie, vice president of product and technical marketing at MinIO.
“On the data lake side, I think it’s hard to overstate just what a big deal Iceberg has been,” he told theCUBE. “If you think back, it’s not that long ago that every database had its own proprietary format. The idea of an open table format was just bonkers … but we are really seeing now the incredible widespread adoption. That’s enabled us to do really clever things like integrating support for Iceberg into the storage tier.”
That flexibility must extend to documents, images, logs and other unstructured information spread across the enterprise. Coordinating access and movement across the data estate requires several complementary layers: Supermicro’s validated systems, Hammerspace Inc.’s unified namespace and data orchestration, Cloudian Inc.’s object storage and Seagate Technology LLC’s capacity for longer-term retention. Together, those components support a data life cycle spanning active AI use and archival storage, emphasized Sherry Lin, senior product manager of SDS solution at Supermicro. Governance remains essential throughout that life cycle, noted Peter Sjoberg, vice president of worldwide solution architects at Cloudian.
“We see a key goal to put that unstructured data under management so that it is protected, it is safe and secure,” Sjoberg said. “That’s exactly what we’re doing now as this data has moved into the AI era. That data will need to move for different purposes, and you will need to make sure it’s always under your control, unstructured or otherwise, so that you can bring it to your AI needs.”

Supermicro begins shipping liquid-cooled NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks
Photo: panumas nikhomkhai / Wikimedia Commons (Pexels)
Super Micro Computer announced on September 23, 2026 that it has begun shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks integrated with its Data Center Building Block Solutions and DLC-2 direct-liquid-cooling systems. Each rack combines 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs in eighteen 1U compute trays linked by nine sixth-generation NVLink switch trays for 216 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth, delivering 20.7 TB of HBM4 memory and up to 54 TB of LPDDR5X memory. A Scalable Unit Blueprint covers 16 compute racks with 1,152 Rubin GPUs and 331 TB of HBM4; cooling includes 1.8 MW in-row CDUs with N+1 redundancy and optional rear door heat exchangers. Supermicro states its DLC-2 stack achieves 98+% heat capture and sizes the unit at 227 kW per rack with 1 MW cooling towers.
President and CEO Charles Liang said the firm spent years building the liquid-cooling stack, manufacturing capacity, and deployment teams for this moment, and that customers can now order a Scalable Unit and receive production-ready systems with end-to-end integration because the company designs and builds every layer between the cold plate and the cooling tower. NVIDIA’s May 31, 2026 GTC Taipei announcement named Supermicro among system builders in full-scale production, with shipments set to begin in the fall. Contested: none found. The announcement names no customers and gives no order figures or revenue impact.

Don’t Fall for Supermicro’s Margin Magic: The Company Already Said It’s Temporary
Supermicro's gross margin just shattered expectations, sending shares surging, but management quietly buried a number in the earnings call that changes everything investors think they just bought.
Published September 8, 2026, 7:10am ET · 3 min read
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Rows of illuminated servers in a data center symbolize the robust AI infrastructure provided by companies like Super Micro Computer, critical for advancing technological frontiers. © BalticServers.com
Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI | SMCI Price Prediction) closed most recently at $39.59, up 25.8% over one month and 27.9% year to date, yet still 1.1% lower over the trailing year. The rally traces to a fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 report in which non-GAAP gross margin blew past guidance. Did investors buy a structural margin reset or a one-quarter timing artifact? As it turns out, management answered that question on the earnings call.
The bull case is genuine. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $1.70 against a $0.9575 estimate, revenue grew 93.16% year over year, and CEO Charles Liang cited “more than $60 billion in new orders, and booked record backlog entering fiscal 2027.” Full fiscal 2027 revenue guidance is $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion. Some of last week’s strength was sector-driven; TradingView, on September 4, 2026, headlined the story “Supermicro’s Revenue Boom Just Ran Into a Profit Test.”
Reported non-GAAP gross margin was 17.6% versus guidance of 8.2% to 8.4%, a 750 basis point sequential jump. CFO David Weigand said favorable mix “contributed approximately 75% of the gross margin improvement,” with the remainder attributable to lower tariff costs and lower inventory reserves, which he called a “non-recurring event.” The mix itself was inflated by “the deferral of several contracts from Q4 fiscal year 26 to Q1 fiscal year 27.” Lower-margin revenue slipping out lifts the percentage without improving the business. Liang said, “This margin expansion mainly came from our strategy focused on balancing customer mix and product mix while having a one-time positive contribution for the quarter.” Revenue landed near the low end of the $11 billion to $12.5 billion range on customer readiness delays. Miss on top line, beat on margin, same cause.
Management guided current-quarter non-GAAP gross margin to 10.4% to 10.8%, well below the reported 17.6%. A quiet period begins at the close of business on Friday, September 11, 2026, so this number stands.
Customer diversification is genuine. David Weigand noted nine customers with revenues greater than $1 billion each in fiscal year 2026, versus four in fiscal year 2025. Full-year revenue reached $39.06 billion (+77.8% year over year). (That kind of concentration in AI server buildouts is why we keep pointing readers to the power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the data centers in a free report.)
Offsetting this is that fiscal 2026 operating cash flow was negative $6.81 billion, closing inventory rose to $12.9 billion, and the cash conversion cycle (days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers) lengthened materially. A company can grow revenue while consuming cash when it prepays inventory faster than customers pay invoices.
Supermicro raised $5.6 billion in public equity, including $4.2 billion in mandatory convertible preferred (shares that automatically convert to common). The guided non-GAAP diluted share count is 761 million. David Weigand said EPS is now computed using the two-class method, allocating a portion of net income to participating convertible preferred shares.
Gross margin must hold against the new 10.4% to 10.8% guidance. The deferred contracts must land without dragging margin lower when they do. The $65.0 billion to $72.0 billion revenue range must survive a quarter of contact, and growth must start generating operating cash. This thesis will be disproved by any quarter in which revenue grows and gross margin lands at or below the full prior-year level, or any walk-back of the forward revenue range.
The market bought a margin figure that management, in its own words and its own next-quarter guide, has already told investors will not repeat. Though the growth story is intact and the order book is a genuine asset, the profitability step-up appears transitory.

Why Super Micro (SMCI) Stock Is Up Today
What Happened?
Shares of server solutions provider Super Micro (NASDAQ:SMCI) jumped 4.3% in the afternoon session after the company began shipping server racks built for NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin AI architecture, according to TipRanks. The start of shipments reinforces SMCI's role in the AI infrastructure supply chain. Vera Rubin–ready racks house and interconnect high-density systems that data centers need for advanced AI workloads, keeping the stock in the AI server buildout story.
The shares were trading at $43.69, up 4.4% from the previous close.
Is now the time to buy Super Micro? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.
Super Micro's shares are extremely volatile and have had 69 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 7 months ago when the stock dropped 30.4% on the news that federal prosecutors unsealed a criminal indictment charging a company co-founder and two associates with conspiring to smuggle $2.5 billion in restricted AI servers to China. The Department of Justice alleged the group bypassed U.S. export controls by routing Nvidia-powered systems through Southeast Asian intermediaries and using deceptive labeling to mask the final destination. While Super Micro itself was not named as a defendant, the involvement of high-ranking personnel likely raised scrutiny over the firm's internal compliance and governance frameworks.In response, Super Micro stated it had placed the implicated employees on leave and is cooperating with authorities.
Super Micro is up 41.1% since the beginning of the year, but at $43.69 per share, it is still trading 25.6% below its 52-week high of $58.68 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Super Micro's shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $11,845.

Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI) is Attracting Investor Attention: Here is What You Should Know
Fri, October 2, 2026 at 5:00 AM PDT 5 min read
Super Micro Computer (SMCI) is one of the stocks most watched by Zacks.com visitors lately. So, it might be a good idea to review some of the factors that might affect the near-term performance of the stock.
Over the past month, shares of this server technology company have returned +10.7%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's +0.6% change. During this period, the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry, which Super Micro falls in, has gained 11.5%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?
Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.
Rather than focusing on anything else, we at Zacks prioritize evaluating the change in a company's earnings projection. This is because we believe the fair value for its stock is determined by the present value of its future stream of earnings.
Our analysis is essentially based on how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to take the latest business trends into account. When earnings estimates for a company go up, the fair value for its stock goes up as well. And when a stock's fair value is higher than its current market price, investors tend to buy the stock, resulting in its price moving upward. Because of this, empirical studies indicate a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and short-term stock price movements.
For the current quarter, Super Micro is expected to post earnings of $1.06 per share, indicating a change of +202.9% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed -1.1% over the last 30 days.
For the current fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $4.37 points to a change of +20.4% from the prior year. Over the last 30 days, this estimate has remained unchanged.
For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $5.13 indicates a change of +17.5% from what Super Micro is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has remained unchanged.
With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool -- the Zacks Rank -- is a more conclusive indicator of a stock's near-term price performance, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Super Micro.
The chart below shows the evolution of the company's forward 12-month consensus EPS estimate:
12-month consensus EPS estimate for SMCI
While earnings growth is arguably the most superior indicator of a company's financial health, nothing happens as such if a business isn't able to grow its revenues. After all, it's nearly impossible for a company to increase its earnings for an extended period without increasing its revenues. So, it's important to know a company's potential revenue growth.
For Super Micro, the consensus sales estimate for the current quarter of $14.81 billion indicates a year-over-year change of +195.1%. For the current and next fiscal years, $67.01 billion and $78.82 billion estimates indicate +71.5% and +17.6% changes, respectively.
Last Reported Results and Surprise History
Super Micro reported revenues of $11.12 billion in the last reported quarter, representing a year-over-year change of +93.2%. EPS of $1.7 for the same period compares with $0.41 a year ago.
Compared to the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $11 billion, the reported revenues represent a surprise of +1.09%. The EPS surprise was +150%.
The company beat consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters. The company topped consensus revenue estimates two times over this period.
Without considering a stock's valuation, no investment decision can be efficient. In predicting a stock's future price performance, it's crucial to determine whether its current price correctly reflects the intrinsic value of the underlying business and the company's growth prospects.
Comparing the current value of a company's valuation multiples, such as its price-to-earnings (P/E), price-to-sales (P/S), and price-to-cash flow (P/CF), to its own historical values helps ascertain whether its stock is fairly valued, overvalued, or undervalued, whereas comparing the company relative to its peers on these parameters gives a good sense of how reasonable its stock price is.
The Zacks Value Style Score (part of the Zacks Style Scores system), which pays close attention to both traditional and unconventional valuation metrics to grade stocks from A to F (an A is better than a B; a B is better than a C; and so on), is pretty helpful in identifying whether a stock is overvalued, rightly valued, or temporarily undervalued.
Super Micro is graded B on this front, indicating that it is trading at a discount to its peers. Click here to see the values of some of the valuation metrics that have driven this grade.
The facts discussed here and much other information on Zacks.com might help determine whether or not it's worthwhile paying attention to the market buzz about Super Micro. However, its Zacks Rank #2 does suggest that it may outperform the broader market in the near term.

Cisco Stock Gains 2% as Supermicro Servers Enter Its AI Factory Channel
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO), the networking, security and observability company, rose approximately 2.0% to $115.08 at 11.14am ET on October 6 as its planned October rollout brings Supermicro GPU systems into its authorized sales channel. The pitch is bigger than faster switches: Cisco wants customers buying the infrastructure around their AI workloads, too. The valuation picture shows shares 53.26% above the $75.09 GF Value estimate, leaving a hefty premium for that growth story to justify.
Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with CSCO.

Cisco Stock Gains 2% as Supermicro Servers Enter Its AI Factory Channel · us.finance.gurufocus
Customers can buy liquid- or air-cooled Supermicro servers alongside Cisco networking, distributed security and Splunk observability. Cisco's architecture FAQ describes validation services designed to check the complete system against reference designs before deployment. That could ease the work of getting expensive GPU clusters running. But the launch documents provide no system pricing, partner economics or orders tied specifically to the expanded package.
The demand backdrop has substance. According to Reuters, Cisco booked $9.3 billion of hyperscaler AI-infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026, while management projects $7.5 billion of related revenue in fiscal 2027. The next test is whether this broader offering wins meaningful business from enterprises, neoclouds and sovereign clouds. Investors need to see how much Cisco networking, security and software each deployment carriesand how much profit those sales produce.

A retouching company insider considers "PhotoCraft," an open-source Photoshop alternative｜東京レタッチ公式ノート", "published": "", "text": "Is the "Adobe Tax" high? A retouching company insider considers "PhotoCraft," an open-source Photoshop alternative
"Crafting Apps," which aims to provide alternatives to seven Adobe applications including Photoshop and Illustrator, has been released. It is free and open-source, and the image editing software PhotoCraft claims to support reading and saving PSD files.
"Seven apps. One craft." (Official English translation)
Crafting Apps: open-source creative tools
Image editing, vector illustration, video, photography, PDFs,
For those of us who keep paying for Adobe subscriptions, this is an intriguing project. If we can do the same work while reducing expenses, we would want to consider switching.
We have 50 retouchers at our company. Honestly, I would be happy if the amount paid for subscriptions could be reduced. However, as a company that works as a team on retouching for photo books and merchandise, we cannot switch based on price alone. We need to verify whether we can continue our current workflow, from editing to quality control, revisions, and delivery.
PhotoCraft is still in early alpha. Even so, I am interested in how far this software can go as a substitute for Photoshop. If we call the burden of continuing to pay Adobe the "Adobe tax," what are the conditions for reducing those payments? I will consider the public information on PSD compatibility in light of our work.
What is PhotoCraft | Free Photoshop alternative software and development status
PhotoCraft is a free, open-source image editing software released by the ArtCraft team. The official website highlights editing features such as layers, masks, adjustment layers, and text, as well as support for reading and saving PSD and PSB files.
The explanation that it supports image editing and the exchange of Photoshop files piques my interest in it as a professional alternative. This is because I can envision uses ranging from completing images on my own to taking over existing PSD files.
"You can open and save PSD/PSB documents with layers." (Official English translation)
PhotoCraft: The image editor you already know how to use.
The open-source image editor you already know how to use.
However, the current GitHub README explicitly states that it is in an early alpha stage and is not yet a replacement for Photoshop in daily professional work. When reading the feature list, one must also consider this stage of development.
"It is not yet a replacement for Photoshop in daily professional work." (README English translation)
What are Crafting Apps | 7 Adobe alternative apps and their corresponding uses
PhotoCraft is part of a project by ArtCraft called "Crafting Apps." Seven apps are being released that aim to serve the same purposes as Adobe products, ranging from image editing to video, PDF, and page layout.
The official team has set a policy of building from scratch using the Rust programming language, releasing it as free open-source software, and processing files locally. A programming language is a language used to describe the functions and processing of an application. Open-source refers to a form where the source code, which constitutes the design of the software, is made public and can be used, modified, and redistributed according to license conditions.
PhotoCraft and PrintCraft are positioned as early alpha, while the others are under development. The table shows the correspondence of uses and does not mean that the features or compatibility have become equivalent.
"Each app in Crafting Apps is written from scratch in Rust." (Official English translation)
Crafting Apps: open-source creative tools
Image editing, vector illustration, video, photography, PDFs,
"Not all seven types have become finished products that can directly replace Adobe products"
無料のAdobe代替アプリ集「ArtCraft Crafting Apps」、オープンソースでPhotoshop・Illustrator・Premiere・Lightroom・Acrobat・After Effects・InDesignの代替を目指す
AIによる画像・動画制作ソフトを開発するArtCraftが、Adobe Creative Cloudのクリエイティブツール
ArtCraft's operating company and number of employees | Publicly stated size is 2-10 people
ArtCraft is a project operated by a company, but it is also worth looking at the scale of that company. According to the Artcraft AI LinkedIn company profile, the headquarters is in Atlanta, Georgia, USA, and the employee size is listed as '2-10 employees'.
'Company size: 2-10 employees' (Japanese translation of the company profile)

ArtCraft provides artificial intelligence (AI) tools for arti
'2-10 people' is a size category on the company profile. It does not indicate the exact number of current staff, the number of developers dedicated to PhotoCraft, or the number of external collaborators. Furthermore, the collation of the corporate name in the old terms of service with the current ArtCraft registration information has not been completed. The funding amount is also a different figure from capital or sales.
Even so, knowing that a project aiming for seven Adobe alternative apps is coming from a company of this publicly stated size changes how one perceives it. Both expectations for what can be built by a small team and questions about the structure for continuously developing and maintaining multiple apps arise.
We have 50 retouchers. Since our job types are different, we cannot simply compare by number of people, but if we were to move our work foundation, in addition to the ability to create features, I would also want to confirm the structure that can continue updates, bug fixes, and inquiries. Quality is not determined by numbers alone. However, it is material for making an adoption decision that was not visible just by the fact that it can be used for free.
PhotoCraft pricing and operation | Is it free now, and will there be a charge in the future?
Currently, Crafting Apps, including PhotoCraft, is officially advertised as being available for free.
'It can be used for free.' (Japanese translation of the official statement)
Crafting Apps: open-source creative tools
Image editing, vector illustration, video, photography, PDFs,
ArtCraft is a project operated by a company. Its former name was Storyteller AI, and Learning Machines, Inc. is listed as the operating corporation in the official Storyteller terms of service. They also provide paid image and video generation services. The official pricing page explains that subscription revenue supports the provision of free, open-source offerings. It must be viewed as a business that combines free apps with paid services.
'Learning Machines, Inc. conducts business under the name Storyteller' (Japanese translation of the terms of service)
However, the free provision of the PhotoCraft app itself and the paid plans or generation credits for image and video generation services are separate charges.
'Your subscriptions help keep ArtCraft free and open for everyone.' (Japanese translation of the pricing page)
ArtCraft is the open-source desktop app for generating AI vid
A guarantee that all new features and services will remain free in the future could not be confirmed in the official app list, the PhotoCraft README, or the pricing page checked this time. The source code for PhotoCraft is released under an open-source license such as MIT or Apache-2.0, but that alone does not determine future service fees or the continuation of updates and support.
Even if it is free now, there is a possibility that future new features, additional services, and support will become paid. The boundary between free apps and paid services is not necessarily the same in the future. At this point, no plans to charge for the PhotoCraft app itself have been confirmed.
If we were to consider switching, as a work foundation used by 50 retouchers, I would also want to see where costs might arise in the future. In addition to current pricing and quality, I would want to confirm whether the development of necessary features will continue and how they will respond when we are in trouble. From the fact that it is free now, we cannot estimate that costs or operational burdens will disappear in the future.
PhotoCraft bug response | Differences in support compared to Adobe
Just as concerning as the pricing is the response when work stops due to a bug. In addition to whether it is operated by a company, it is necessary to confirm who can be consulted and how far they will go to provide support.
ArtCraft's official support includes Discord and email channels. PhotoCraft also has a place called GitHub Issues, where you can report bugs and feature requests.
"This is the fastest way to contact us." (Japanese translation of the Discord channel description)
ArtCraft is the open-source desktop app for generating AI vid
However, having a channel is different from being promised a response that meets business deadlines. Based on the public information I checked this time, I could not confirm any response deadlines for inquiries or bug fix timelines for the free version of PhotoCraft. While ArtCraft's paid Enterprise plan includes information regarding service level agreements for support, that cannot be treated as a condition that applies to the free PhotoCraft.
In addition to customer support channels, Adobe provides support for administrators of group and enterprise versions. You also need to check the scope of support included in those contracts. It does not mean that every bug in Adobe will be fixed immediately.
"Expert support for your issues." (Japanese translation of the inquiry channel description)
In a company like ours with 50 retouchers, we need a way to continue deliveries while waiting for fixes. Can we work in a different version, revert to Photoshop to continue, or preserve the original data? I want to verify these countermeasures before implementation. Even if the subscription becomes cheaper, if it takes internal time to investigate or work around bugs, we have to compare including that burden.
PhotoCraft's AI Integration | Automation of Editing Tasks and Quality Assurance
A design that allows editing functions to be operated by AI agents is also a feature touted by the official source. For a company like ours that handles images as a team, we want to consider not just the cost, but also how much of the work can be automated. However, just because it supports automated operations does not lead to the conclusion that we can entrust it with quality checks as well. I would want to separately verify whether it can produce results that meet our common retouching standards.
"Built for automation and AI agents." (Official Japanese translation)
Crafting Apps: open-source creative tools
Image editing, vector illustration, video, photography, PDFs,
PhotoCraft's PSD Compatibility | Differences in Reading/Writing, Rendering, and Editing
The official PhotoCraft website explains that out of 135 actual test files, 134 can be maintained down to the byte level through a round trip of reading and writing. Reading just this creates the expectation that you can handle Photoshop files as they are.
"134 out of 135 actual test files remain byte-for-byte identical through a round trip." (Official Japanese translation)
PhotoCraft: The image editor you already know how to use.
The open-source image editor you already know how to use.
However, the current GitHub README explains it in a bit more detail. Rendering consistency when opened and re-saved in the app is stated as 307 out of 309 in one test group, and 169 out of 170 in another. On the other hand, it also states that files re-saved from the app do not match the original files at the byte level.
What explains byte-level reproduction is a test of independent components that read and write PSDs without going through the document editing model.
"Re-saved files do not match the original files at the byte level." (Japanese translation of the README)

Shares of Adobe (ADBE -0.28%) have had a tough 2026. The stock ended last year at about $350 and trades near $240 as I write, down about 31%.
The software company has kept buying its own shares on the way down. In April, its board approved a new $25 billion stock buyback authorization, meant partly to "reduce share count over time." It runs through April 30, 2030.
And as Adobe's fiscal third quarter of 2026 ended Aug. 28, $24.55 billion of it was still unused.
Compared with Adobe's market value, the amount is large. With about 389.2 million shares outstanding in mid-September, Adobe is worth about $93 billion at today's stock price. The remaining authorization could buy back about 26% of it -- about 102 million shares.
Sure, an authorization isn't a promise. Adobe has around three and a half years to use it, and nothing forces the company to spend it all. But I think the company's pace this year shows it plans to put plenty of it to work.
Image source: Getty Images.
In the fiscal year's first three quarters, Adobe's buybacks averaged around $2.3 billion a quarter. That came to $6.82 billion, for 26.1 million shares, all bought on the open market.
And as the stock dropped, the same money bought more shares. The 9.5 million shares Adobe repurchased in fiscal Q3 cost an average of around $235 each, versus about $261 over all three quarters.
Notably, the company paid for it with cash from its operations. Adobe generated $7.65 billion of cash from operations during the same stretch, up around 11% year over year, and buybacks used close to 90% of it. Its balance sheet had $5.64 billion of cash and short-term investments at quarter-end, versus around $6.4 billion of debt.
This pace leaves room to spare. Spreading the unspent $24.55 billion evenly through April 2030 comes out to around $7 billion a year, about what Adobe spent in just those three quarters. If the company keeps buying at its recent rate instead, it could use up the authorization sometime in 2029.
Adobe's diluted share count (the number used to calculate earnings per share) was around 395 million in the fiscal third quarter. That compares to 402 million in the fiscal second quarter and 424 million in the year-ago quarter.
Management's fourth-quarter targets assume around 389 million. In other words, the count's dropping about 2% a quarter, and steadily.
Not every repurchased share sticks, though. Shares outstanding dropped by around 22 million in the nine months, fewer than the 26.1 million Adobe bought, because employee stock awards added some back.
Showing what the shrinking count means for shareholders, Adobe's non-GAAP (adjusted) net income rose around 8% year over year in fiscal Q3 to $2.42 billion. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 15% to $6.13.
On a GAAP basis, net income grew just 3%, but earnings per share climbed 11% to $4.62. In short, fewer shares drove about half of the quarter's adjusted per-share growth.
If Adobe spent all $24.55 billion at roughly $240 a share and its earnings stayed flat, retiring about 26% of its shares would raise earnings per share by over a third.
That won't happen all at once, and the price Adobe pays will move. A lower stock price would stretch the cash further, and a higher one would shrink it.
$93BMarket cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary.
Is the buyback a reason to buy?
At roughly $240, Adobe shares cost about 13 times earnings. Using the midpoint of management's fiscal 2026 target for adjusted earnings per share ($24.45 to $24.50), the price is about 10 times adjusted earnings. When shares reached their 52-week high of $363.70, that same target worked out to almost 15 times adjusted earnings.
I'd say buying back stock at about 10 times adjusted earnings is one of the better uses of Adobe's cash right now.
True, a buyback can't fix slowing growth. Adobe's total annualized recurring revenue (ARR), its gauge of the subscription business on a yearly basis, rose 11.2% year over year in fiscal Q3, and management's full-year target is 10.2%. And the market's discount probably reflects worries that artificial intelligence tools might hurt Adobe's pricing power. But as long as the subscription business keeps growing, a falling share count should help earnings per share outpace the business itself.
All in all, I think the buyback makes a cheap stock more interesting. Adobe stock looks worth considering at this price, but I'd want the subscription business to keep growing at roughly its current pace.

When research involves long PDFs, finding a relevant passage can take considerable time. We might remember a finding without recalling its location, or need to compare how several papers address the same question. In this Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant review, I examine its summaries, document questions, source links, and uses for educators and researchers.
Its appeal is the connection between the response and the document. I would use that connection to locate evidence and guide reading, while checking whether the cited material supports the answer.
What Is Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant?
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant provides conversational tools for working with documents in Acrobat. It lets users ask questions, generate summaries, and explore collections through PDF Spaces.
It fits research reading and document analysis. For a literature review, I would use it after collecting suitable sources, alongside a reference manager and my own reading notes.
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant Review: Main Features
You can open a PDF, select AI Assistant, and type a question or choose a suggested one. Adobe’s documentation describes answers with source citations and follow-up suggestions.
For researchers, useful questions might include:
What research question does this paper address?
How did the authors select their participants?
Which limitations do they acknowledge?
Where do they explain this finding?
I would begin with a specific question tied to the document. Asking where the authors discuss a limitation is more manageable than requesting a judgement about whether the entire study is trustworthy.
Adobe’s AI Assistant instructions explain that selecting a source number takes you to the relevant section.
This is one of the features I would prioritize when evaluating a research-reading tool. It gives us a practical route for checking the response against the paper.
However, a citation does not establish that an answer is accurate. Read the surrounding passage, examine qualifications, and check whether the response has converted a tentative claim into a definite conclusion.
Also distinguish these document citations from bibliographic references. A link to a passage helps verify an answer; it does not automatically provide the reference entry required for a manuscript.
Acrobat’s Generative Summary produces an overview with section headings and summaries. Adobe also describes cross-references that let readers move from the summary to the corresponding source section.
I would use this to plan a reading session. After reviewing the overview, identify the sections most relevant to your question and examine them directly.
For empirical papers, check whether the summary preserves the relationship between the method and the conclusion. A finding makes more sense when we know who participated, what was measured, and what the design can establish.
PDF Spaces brings related files into a shared workspace where users can ask questions across the content. Adobe’s documentation lists support for organizing up to 100 files in a space, adding notes, saving useful responses, and sharing the workspace.
For research, I would begin with a small collection around a clearly defined question. Ask how the papers define a concept or how their methods differ, then check the relevant documents individually.
A larger collection can be convenient, but it also creates more opportunities to merge findings that should remain separate. Keep study populations, settings, and measures visible when comparing sources.
Related: Zotero Reference Management Review
Use audio overviews and share reading collections
Adobe also offers podcast-style document overviews and sharing options through PDF Spaces.
An audio overview could help someone revisit a collection before a meeting or identify sections to read later. It should be treated as another generated representation of the sources.
Sharing could support a research team or graduate reading group. I would agree on the collection’s purpose and permissions before inviting others. A shared workspace is most useful when contributors know which sources belong there and what notes they should add.

Prepare for detailed reading. Generate an overview, identify relevant sections, and read them yourself. Note where the overview omits information needed to interpret the findings.
Compare study methods. Ask about sampling, data collection, or outcome measures across a small set of papers. Verify each comparison before incorporating it into your literature review.
Recover evidence during writing. Use a question to locate the passage behind a note or claim. Check the original wording before quoting or paraphrasing it.
Prepare a research meeting. Gather selected papers in a PDF Space and save questions that need discussion. Keep unresolved issues visible.
These are suggested workflows, whose value depends on the documents, the questions, and the accuracy of the responses.
Teachers could use Acrobat AI Assistant to introduce source-checking activities. Students first read a short section, then examine an AI answer and its cited passage. Ask them whether the passage supports the answer and which qualifications need to be retained.
Another activity could compare a generated summary with the original abstract or conclusion. Students identify what each version emphasizes and what they need to read elsewhere in the paper.
For graduate seminars, a small PDF Space could support discussion of methodological differences. The task should require students to explain those differences using the original studies.
Full access is available through eligible Acrobat plans or an AI Assistant add-on. Adobe’s current offerings include plans such as Acrobat Express and Acrobat Studio, while institutional access may depend on licensing and administrator settings.
Check the official plans page for your country and account type. Pricing, included features, and billing commitments vary, so a displayed monthly figure should be read alongside its annual or monthly contract terms.
Before purchasing, confirm whether your institution already provides access. A standard Acrobat subscription should not be assumed to include every AI feature.
Adobe’s technical requirements, checked on October 1, 2026, list files below 100 MB and up to 600 pages. PDFs should not have password protection or usage restrictions. An internet connection and a supported Adobe account are required.
The requirements also state that AI Assistant does not support images or complex vector graphics. This matters when interpreting research figures: do not assume that an answer about a document includes a reliable analysis of its charts.
Language support varies by feature and platform. Check the current requirements when working with multilingual literature.
Adobe states that customer content is not used to train the generative AI models delivering Acrobat features. That statement still needs to be considered alongside institutional rules for confidential materials and document sharing. In PDF Spaces, inspect access permissions before distributing a collection.
Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant is worth considering if much of your research reading already happens in Acrobat. Questions, summaries, and PDF Spaces offer several ways to navigate documents while keeping sources accessible.
I would assess it using papers you already know. Check whether answers point to supporting passages, summaries preserve limitations, and comparisons keep studies distinct. Those checks provide a more useful basis for choosing the tool than the fluency of its responses.

Adobe's ChatGPT plugin gains interactive editors for images, designs, and PDFs. Users can brush a selection, tweak sliders, and edit PDF text from side panels in the ChatGPT window.
Following last week’s addition of tools into Google Gemini and expansion of Claude capabilities, Adobe has now added interactive editing experiences to the Adobe plugin in ChatGPT. Announced alongside OpenAI's DevDay 2026 unveils, the new capabilities cover images, designs, and PDFs, and appear in side panels in the ChatGPT chat window.
The image and design editors are powered by Photoshop and Adobe Express. Users can select part of an image in the interactive editor, ask ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to make changes, then fine-tune the result with new controls. They can pick out objects or brush over areas, then adjust hue, saturation, contrast, and more with sliders.

To make the latte pop more, focus on the cup again with the brush tool and ask ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to adjust its brightness and contrast. Adobe dynamically surfaces sliders for both, so you can fine-tune the image to get the look you're going for.”
PDFs, meanwhile, open in a side panel using Acrobat tools. Users can revise text or highlight passages in place, then send that document context back to ChatGPT to continue the task.
In one example that will hit home with plenty of people, a user highlights a paragraph about payment terms in a freelance contract and asks ChatGPT to use the Adobe plugin to highlight other sections about payments or invoicing.

While Apple has long offered iMovie for iPhone and iPad, Google has never had a comparable offering. Adobe is now stepping up to fill this feature gap with a proper version of Premiere. The app is now available in the Play Store for almost all Android devices, and it’s free (mostly).
Android’s version of Premiere doesn’t offer all the features you’d get in the desktop application, but it’s a big step up from the soon-to-be-retired Premiere Rush app. You can import as many video tracks as you want, trim them, split them, add effects, and export videos in up to 4K resolution. It can even extract audio from clips, reduce background noise, and add voiceovers. The app emphasizes the YouTube Short format, even defaulting your video outputs to portrait 16:9, but you can change that to something more traditional.
On a standard smartphone, the app splits the screen with the timeline at the bottom and preview up top. Adobe says that Premiere is optimized for multiple form factors. If you have a foldable phone, the UI adjusts to give you more breathing room, placing the timeline to the right of the video. That makes sense as the default, as Premiere wants you to make YouTube Shorts, but if you’re working with something wider, there’s a layout toggle that puts the widescreen video above the expanded timeline. The split is also adjustable if you want to make your video or timeline larger.
I tested Premiere by importing multiple high-bitrate 4K clips, and it didn’t choke. However, processing newly added video tracks can take a minute. Exporting is also not instant, but it’s faster than I expected on a Pixel, which isn’t exactly known for extreme performance. A three-minute 4K60 video in high-quality mode took about three minutes. The app is designed to work on any Android device with at least 5GB of RAM.

There are a good number of options in the editing interface—unless you’re a pro or enthusiast video editor, this app should be more than powerful enough. Adobe also says that Premiere (and the rest of its mobile app portfolio) is optimized for Googlebook laptops. If you need more, there’s always the full desktop version of Premiere. Of course, that won’t be an option on Googlebooks.
Premiere for Android is free, and you don’t even need a subscription or Creative Cloud account unless you care about generative AI tools. The new Premiere app has image-to-video and text-to-video, with options for Adobe’s “commercial safe” Firefly model as well as Google Veo, Google Omni, Luma Ray, and Kling models.
You can generate some clips for free in Premiere, which comes with 250 monthly AI credits. That’s enough for a few Veo Fast clips (80 credits each) or a single Firefly video. For $70 per year or $8 per month, you get 1,200 monthly AI credits in the Premiere mobile app. If that’s not your thing, you can just enjoy the free, vastly improved video editing experience on Android. Apple devices got this app last year, but “better late than never” has always been the Android app motto.

Investing.com -- Goldman Sachs maintained its "sell" rating on Adobe as Anil Chakravarthy prepares to take over as president and CEO on Dec. 1, saying competition is intensifying and new entrants are gaining ground in areas that could expand Adobe's market.

The broker said it wants clearer evidence of Adobe's strategy and execution before changing its view. It sees the leadership change as a potential catalyst, but said the market remains concerned that artificial intelligence could weigh on Adobe's growth.
Chakravarthy's appointment follows a transition announced in March. He previously led Adobe's Customer Experience Orchestration business and worldwide field operations. David Wadhwani, who headed the Creativity & Productivity business, is also leaving to start a new venture, while Adobe is appointing a permanent chief financial officer.
Goldman said a successful turnaround will depend on Adobe simplifying its product architecture, speeding up innovation through internal investment and targeted acquisitions, and converting adoption of new features into revenue. The key question is whether the new management makes significant strategic changes or largely extends the existing three- to five-year plan.

Firefly: Adobe has shifted from relying mainly on its own Firefly models toward using Creative Cloud as a platform that brings together multiple third-party AI models.
Goldman said this moves Adobe's focus from competing on AI model quality to controlling the workflow. Firefly initially stood out because its models were trained on Adobe Stock, licensed content and public-domain material.
Acquisitions: Goldman expects Adobe to pursue smaller deals that add technology and engineering talent rather than make a large transformational acquisition.
It pointed to Salesforce and Workday as examples of companies taking a similar approach, although potential targets could command high valuations.
User growth: Monthly active users across Acrobat, Creative Cloud, Express and Firefly exceeded 1 billion in the third quarter, up more than 20% from a year earlier.
Adobe is seeking to turn that growth into revenue through free-to-paid conversions, higher-priced plans such as CC Pro and charges for users who exceed their included generative AI credits.
Express: Goldman said Adobe's uneven product development has left Express trailing Canva, which has more than 265 million monthly users and at least $4 billion in annual recurring revenue. Goldman estimated Express had about 70 million monthly users in 2025.
Customer experience: Adobe is repositioning Experience Cloud, which accounts for about a quarter of subscription revenue and is growing at a low-teens rate excluding Semrush, as a platform for managing AI-driven customer experiences.
Goldman said it remains unclear whether this orchestration role can become a valuable business in its own right or mainly serves to protect Adobe's existing software products.

Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE | ADBE Price Prediction) is a Hold at $235.47. Shares of the creative software leader trade as if the business were in decline, yet the company keeps raising its guidance.
Adobe makes Photoshop, Premiere, Acrobat and a customer experience suite that serves over 20,000 global enterprises. Third-quarter revenue rose 12.9% to $6.76 billion. Non-GAAP EPS of $6.13 was its 5th consecutive EPS beat. The stock still fell 32.72% year to date. Investors worry about generative AI rivals, a CEO transition to Anil Chakravarthy and the exit of the company’s former CFO.
Nine Times Forward Earnings for a Double-Digit Grower
Bulls see a mispricing. Adobe trades at 9x forward earnings with a PEG ratio of 0.582. Management raised its full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance from an initial $23.30 to $23.50 to $24.45 to $24.50. AI-first ARR now tops $650 million and is growing more than 150%, which shows that customers pay for Firefly and agentic tools.
Capital returns support the case. Free cash flow rose 14.68% to $2.44 billion, and Adobe retired ~9.5M shares for $2.232B with approximately $24.55 billion of authorization remaining. On the insider side, Director David Ricks purchased 10,000 shares at $194.513 on the open market.
AI Rivals and Leadership Churn Test Adobe’s Moat
Bears point to profits lagging sales. Net income grew just 3.1% in the quarter, while RPO growth slowed to 8%. Management put Creative Cloud price increases on hold to guide users into freemium, and it said that the shift pressures net new ARR.
Competition is getting louder. One widely discussed Reddit post read: “OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5. I expect Adobe stocks to nosedive once mass media gets a hold of this.” Add a $70M goodwill impairment in Publishing and Advertising, and the market views a business in transition.
A New CEO’s First Moves Decide the Next Leg
Adobe’s execution rules out a Sell, and the unclear AI outlook rules out a Buy. The stock sits below its 50-day average of $257.41 and its 200-day average of $263.2, so momentum has not turned. The next few months bring Adobe MAX, Chakravarthy’s first strategy statements as CEO, the close of the Topaz Labs deal and a seasonally strong fourth quarter.
Across 40 analysts, the average price target is $278.15, which implies about 18.1% upside. Price targets reflect analysts’ views and often miss. The ratings break down as follows:
The stock trades at 13x trailing earnings, inside a 52-week range of $190.12 to $363.7. Over the past year, Adobe fell 33.51% while the S&P 500 rose 17.22%. Over the past month, the stock dropped 13.9% against a 0.69% rose for the index.
At $235.47, Adobe is a Hold.
The valuation already prices in a lot of bad news, but buying the stock needs a reason for it to rebound. The first trigger for a Buy is fourth-quarter results that meet guidance of $6.80B to $6.85B in revenue with a margin near 44.0%, together with a increase in RPO growth. The second is proof that freemium users, now over 100 million on the creative side alone, are turning into paying subscribers.
A Sell case would build if ARR growth misses the 10.2% target or if analysts cut fiscal 2027 estimates, which currently average 27.6226. Because the stock has a beta of 1.417, it can swing sharply in either direction.
Waiting costs little. The stock pays no dividend, and the new CEO’s first full quarter will show whether Adobe’s AI spending leads to profit growth. At this price, patience lets investors see the new CEO’s results before taking a position.
